messages.author: 0a2394afd48d5894
messages.subject: Box plot based dashboard.
parts:
Hello all,

I am trying to create a dashboard report using ggplot2. My goal is to have something similar to this (follow here for macro picture):


The input is historical data for multiple variable. 
Grey area marks the range, Blue 1 standard deviation from the mean (in general boxplot, jost styled differently)

Yellow arrow marks the most recent value. 

Any ideas on the most efficient way to go with it?

At the moment i have two datasets:
1. Dataset with historical values for each variable
2. Summary dataset for each variable (with min, max, mean, SD, and last vale extracted)

Thanks in advance.
To

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Box plot based dashboard.
parts:
To, 

Since you have min and max values and can compute on the fly the SD min/max values you could use multiple layers of geom_bar and then perhaps a dot for the current value. Putting all of the values on the chart could probably be done with geom_text, but it likely won't look at pretty without some serious tuning/modifications. 

Supply your summary dataset and perhaps someone can get you started. 

Brandon

Thanks for the answer.

I have an issue however.

My simplified dataset is like this:

> Name <- c("Yield", "Spread")
> Mean <- c(6.47, -0.01)
> SD <- c(2.38, 0.92)
> Min <- c(1.46, -2.45)
> Max <- c(15.48, 2.81)
> Last <- c(2.19, 1.51)
> Data <- data.frame(Name, Mean, SD, Min, Max, Last)

The problem I have is that some of the variables have means bellow 0 and, what could make Bar option more problematic. I have also thought on mapping each variable to same scale, where min is 0 and max is 1 and use actual values as labels, however haven't tried yet.

If someone would like to try play with it a little, I would highly appreciate it. I will share more of my code once I have it.

My current version using full data series (data frame with Date in the 1st col and variable in 2nd) is:

> DataM <- melt(Data, id.var="Date", na.rm = T)
> DataM$Last <- FALSE
> DataM$Last[DataM$Date == max(DataM$Date)] <- T
> 
> Plot <- ggplot(DataM, aes(x = variable, y = value)) + 
+             geom_boxplot() + 
+             coord_flip() +
+             scale_x_discrete()
> Plot <- Plot + layer(
+     geom = "point",
+     data = DataM[DataM$Last==T,],
+     geom_params = list(colour = "steelblue",
+                        size=4
+     )
+     )
> Plot


Result of that code is here:



Thanks,
To

messages.author: 0a2394afd48d5894
messages.subject: Re: Box plot based dashboard.
parts:
Thank you guys for recommendations my attempt worked out perfectly (see code bellow), however I ran into other problem that is I beleive related with the way Ggplot2 handles data:

I run this function to generate graph for each variable:
DashPlot <- function(Name, Mean, SD, Min, Max, Last){
    R1 <- Mean - SD
    R2 <- Mean + SD
    Range <- Max-Min
    Plot <- ggplot() + 
        geom_rect(mapping=aes(xmin=Min, xmax=Max, ymin=0, ymax=1.4), fill="lightblue")
    list(is.numeric(Min), Plot)
}

DashPlot("U.S. Treasury note 10 Year Yield", 6.47, 2.38, 1.46, 15.48, 2.19)

While function works, if I have variables Name, Mean, SD, Min, Max, Last defined in the global environment, it seems not to find it if I attempt to submit values through the function.
Any ideas why it can be the case?

[[1]]
[1] TRUE

[[2]]
Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'Min' not found


For those who might be interested in design problem, successful dashboard plot and code are here:



Plot <- ggplot() + 
    geom_rect(mapping=aes(xmin=Min, xmax=Max, ymin=0, ymax=1.4), fill="white") +
    geom_rect(mapping=aes(xmin=Min, xmax=Max, ymin=0, ymax=1), fill="#DCDCDC") +
    geom_rect(mapping=aes(xmin=R1, xmax=R2, ymin=0, ymax=1), fill="#7EC0EE") +
    geom_point(mapping=aes(x=Last, y=1), colour="orange", size=5, shape=18) + 
    geom_rect(mapping=aes(xmin=Last-Range/20, xmax=Last+Range/20, ymin=1, ymax=1.4), fill="orange") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks=sort(c(Min,R1,R2,Max))) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks=NULL) +
    xlab(paste(Name)) + ylab("")
        
Plot <- Plot + theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
                         legend.position="none",
                         axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9),
                         axis.title.x= element_text(size = 9, colour="#515151"))

Plot <- Plot + annotate("text", label = paste(Last), x = Last, y = 1.2, size = 3, colour = "white")+
        annotate("text", label = "Typical", x = Mean, y = 0.5, size = 5, colour = "white")

messages.subject: Re: Box plot based dashboard.
parts:
As I received few private requests to provide a input data for the previously posted code, I decided to post full code that would generate the graph bellow.

library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)

Name <-"Name of the Variable"
Mean <- -0.11
SD <- 0.92
Min <- -2.45
Max <- 2.81
Last <- 1.51

R1 <- Mean - SD
R2 <- Mean + SD
Range <- Max-Min
Plot <- ggplot() +

geom_rect(mapping=aes(xmin=Min, xmax=Max, ymin=0, ymax=1.4), fill="white") +
    geom_rect(mapping=aes(xmin=Min, xmax=Max, ymin=0, ymax=1), fill="#DCDCDC") +
    geom_rect(mapping=aes(xmin=R1, xmax=R2, ymin=0, ymax=1), fill="#7EC0EE") +
    geom_point(mapping=aes(x=Last, y=1), colour="orange", size=5, shape=18) + 
    geom_rect(mapping=aes(xmin=Last-Range/20, xmax=Last+Range/20, ymin=1, ymax=1.4), fill="orange") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks=sort(c(Min,R1,R2,Max))) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks=NULL) +
    xlab(paste(Name)) + ylab("")
PlotA <- Plot + theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),

legend.position="none",
                      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9),
                      axis.title.x= element_text(size = 9, colour="#515151")
)
PlotB <- PlotA + annotate("text", label = paste(Last), x = Last, y = 1.2, size = 3, colour = "white")+
annotate("text", label = "Typical", x = Mean, y = 0.5, size = 5, colour = "white")

ggsave(paste(Name,".jpeg"), PlotB, width = 5, height = 1.4)

t.
